- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., >10% under for 3+ days), sentiment may be bearish — increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment turns neutral or positive.
- Mean reversion is common in 10–15 day horizons — if forecast is 5–10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is weak or flat, model often misses upward momentum — increase forecast by 3–5% if true outcome shows strong upward trend.
- Overshoots after spikes are common in 30-day forecasts — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or 1–2% below 10-day moving average.
